map.An expressions adventure in five chapter: An adventure about expressions in five chapters. It has six reader gates. Solve the math to move the story.
map.Distortion detected. It is rewriting the: Bent patterns found. They are rewriting the city's signs. Reader: stand by.
map.Previously, in Volume Five: the crew's b: Last time, in Volume Five: the crew's blueprints rebuilt the Brightside lot, with its skate ramp, garden beds and stage. The mayor still has Layla's sketch framed. Then the new street signs began to say nonsense.
map.Ms. Ortiz says Ada Vex built a cipher va: Ms. Ortiz says Ada Vex built a cipher vault under the library. The sign machine is inside it.
Ms. Ortiz left us two jars of glow-ink. Each stair lantern uses exactly one third of a jar.
map.So the question is 2 ÷ 1/3. How many thi: So the question is 2 ÷ 1/3. How many third-size servings fit inside two whole jars?
map.The answer to a division is called the q: The answer to a division is called the quotient. Draw a bar for each jar. Slice each bar into thirds. Count the pieces. Models do not lie.
map.Dividing by a fraction asks \"how many o: Dividing by a fraction asks "how many of that piece fit inside?" A bar model shows the pieces. Slice, then count.
map.Two jars of glow-ink. Each stair lantern: Two jars of glow-ink. Each stair lantern uses exactly 1/3 of a jar. Lock A: how many lanterns can the crew light? What is 2 ÷ 1/3? Lock B: the spare 3/4 jar is shared equally among 3 hand-lamps. What is 3/4 ÷ 3?
map.Conceptual: dividing by 1/3 asks 'how ma: Conceptual: dividing by 1/3 asks 'how many third-size servings FIT inside?' Count the slices in the bar model. Sharing among 3 lamps makes each share SMALLER, not bigger.
map.Procedural: Lock A — every jar holds exa: Procedural: Lock A: each jar holds exactly 3 thirds, so count the thirds in BOTH bars. Lock B: dividing by 3 is the same as taking 1/3 of it. Multiply 3/4 × 1/3, then simplify the fraction.
map.There it is — a scribble made of broken: There it is, a scribble made of broken equations. It just wrote "3⁴ = 12" on the wall.
map.Boss fight, level one. It guards the pow: Boss fight, level one. It guards the power cells. Wrong totals keep the lights off.
map.3⁴ is a power: base 3, exponent 4. The e: 3⁴ is a power: base 3, exponent 4. The exponent tells how many times the base is multiplied. It is never base times exponent. The glitch wants you to add or take a shortcut.
map.The glitch scrawled “3⁴ = 12” on the wal: The glitch scribbled “3⁴ = 12” on the wall. Lies. Charge both cells with TRUE totals: Cell A holds 3⁴ crystals, Cell B holds 2⁵.
map.Conceptual: the exponent counts how many: Conceptual: the exponent tells how many copies of the base get MULTIPLIED together. It never multiplies the base directly. That's the glitch's favorite trick.
map.Procedural: write it long. 3⁴ = 3 × 3 ×: Procedural: write it long. 3⁴ = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3. Multiply one step at a time, left to right. Then write five 2s for Cell B and do the same.
map.The sign-press room. A brass machine the: The sign-press room. A brass machine as big as a bus, fed by letter tiles.
map.The press only prints when we feed it Ad: The press only prints when we feed it Ada's sentence. It is written in symbols, not words.
map.Word-to-code translation. The letter n i: Word-to-code time. The letter n is the variable. It is the mystery number in a costume.
map.In a term like 7y, the 7 is the coeffici: In a term like 7y, the 7 is the coefficient. It is the number multiplying the variable. Translate the words, then test your expression with a value.
map.An algebraic expression is math with at: An algebraic expression is math with at least one variable. "Times" becomes a coefficient. "More than" becomes addition.
map.Ada's journal: “5 more than 3 times the: Ada's journal: “5 more than 3 times the mystery number n.” Step 1: pick the expression that says it in symbols. Step 2: test-run the press. Evaluate your expression for n = 4.
map.Conceptual: '3 times n' builds one multi: Conceptual: '3 times n' makes one multiplication term. 3 is the coefficient. '5 more than THAT' adds 5 to the finished product, not to n first.
map.Procedural: translate the 'times' part f: Procedural: write the 'times' part first. Then add the 'more than' part at the end. To evaluate, substitute 4 for n and multiply BEFORE you add.
map.Twin door rule: each pair only powers up: Twin door rule: a pair only powers up if both sides are equivalent expressions: same value for EVERY x.
map.x + x is two sticks taped together — tha: x + x is two sticks taped together. That's 2x. A square of sticks is x·x. Totally different builds.
map.Two tests, crew: distribute and combine: Two tests, crew: distribute and combine like terms, or substitute a number into both sides. Equivalent expressions match every time. The glitch only needs you wrong once.
map.Equivalent expressions name the same val: Equivalent expressions have the same value for every value of the variable. One mismatch = not equivalent.
map.Sort the pairs, reader — true twins powe: Sort the pairs, reader. True twins power the door. Fakes feed the glitch.
map.Four panels, four pairs. Tap a panel to: Four panels, four pairs. Tap a panel to stamp it. First tap: EQUIV (true twins, equal for EVERY x). Second tap: NOT (fake). Third tap clears it. All four stamps must be correct at once.
map.Conceptual: twins agree for EVERY value: Conceptual: twins agree for EVERY value of x. Substitute x = 1, then x = 2, into both sides. One disagreement shows a fake.
map.Procedural: distribute parentheses and c: Procedural: distribute the parentheses and combine like terms before you decide. Remember a(b − c) = ab − ac. The multiplier must hit BOTH terms inside. When in doubt, test a number.
map.The vault's heart: a 24-tooth gear and a: The vault's heart: a 24-tooth gear and a 36-tooth gear. The linking cog must be the greatest common factor. That is the biggest tooth count that divides both.
map.And the timing lights blink every 6 turn: The timing lights blink every 6 turns and every 8 turns. They sync at the least common multiple. That is the first count they share.
map.GCF: the greatest factor two numbers sha: GCF: the greatest factor two numbers share. LCM: the smallest number both count to. Factors divide in. Multiples count up.
map.Size the cog and set the timing, reader: Pick the cog and set the timing, reader. The heart won't turn without you.
map.Two locks turn the heart. Cog lock: the: Two locks turn the heart. Cog lock: the linking cog's tooth count is the GCF of 24 and 36, the greatest count that divides both gears. Timing lock: lights blinking every 6 turns and every 8 turns first sync at their LCM. After how many turns?
map.Conceptual: a GCF divides INTO both numb: Conceptual: a GCF divides INTO both numbers, so it can never be bigger than either gear. An LCM is counted UP TO, so it can never be smaller than either blink number. Factors divide in. Multiples count up.
map.Procedural: list every factor of each ge: Procedural: list every factor of each gear's tooth count. Keep the greatest one they share. Then skip-count by 6s and by 8s until both lists reach the same number.
map.The cipher vault door. The glitch swells: The cipher vault door. The glitch swells and scribbles over Ada's engraving: 18x + 24.
map.Then two more locks: one order-of-operat: Then two more locks: one order-of-operations engine code and one equivalence seal. Reader, forge the master key.
map.Boss Gate: factoring, powers, and equiva: Boss Gate: factoring, powers, and equivalence. Everything this vault taught you, in three locks.
The glitch swells over Ada's engraving. Three locks forge the master key. Lock 1: factor 18x + 24, with the greatest common factor out front. Lock 2: the engine's wake-up code: 2³ × 5 − 10 ÷ 2. Lock 3: stamp the equivalence seal.
map.Conceptual: factoring runs the distribut: Conceptual: factoring runs the distributive property in REVERSE. Pull the greatest common factor out front. What stays inside must multiply back to the original. For the code: powers first, then × and ÷ left to right, subtraction last.
map.Procedural: Lock 1 — find the GCF of 18: Procedural: Lock 1: find the GCF of 18 and 24. Then divide each term by it to fill the parentheses. Lock 2: expand 2³ before anything else. Lock 3: the 4 must multiply BOTH terms inside the parentheses.
map.Vault cleared! The Expression Engine reb: Vault cleared! The Expression Engine restarts. Every sign in the city turns back to honest words.
map.The glitch isn't gone — it's fixed. All: The glitch isn't gone. It's fixed. All its broken equations balanced. Now it's just a tidy little equals sign.
map.Crew captain. Keeps the notebook, asks t: Crew captain. Keeps the notebook and asks the next question. This volume: decoded Ada's journal sentence for the sign press.
map.Evidence officer. Allergic to glitch mat: Evidence officer. Hates glitch math. This volume: caught "3⁴ = 12" red-handed at the power cells.
map.Builder and mixer. This volume: proved x: Builder and mixer. This volume: showed x + x is two sticks, not a square. And found the vault's linking cog.
map.Fragment of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Se: A piece of Ada Vex's Pattern Engine. Senses bent patterns but cannot compute. That's your job.
map.Variable & coefficient.A variable stands: Variable & coefficient.A variable stands for the mystery number. A coefficient multiplies it. "5 more than 3 times n" is 3n + 5. At n = 4 it equals 17.
map.Equivalent expressions.Same value for ev: Equivalent expressions.They have the same value for every variable value: 3(x+4) = 3x+12 and 2x+5x = 7x. But 4(x−2) ≠ 4x−2, and x + x is 2x, not x².
map.Distributive property.Multiply across th: Distributive property.Multiply across the sum. Or run it backwards to factor: 18x + 24 = 6(3x + 4).
map.completed Volume 6: The Expression Engin: completed Volume 6: The Expression Engine and showed skill with fraction division, exponents, writing and evaluating expressions, equivalent expressions, GCF and LCM, and the distributive property.
map.A different crew has 4 jars of lamp oil;: A different crew has 4 jars of lamp oil. Each torch burns 1/2 a jar. Ask: how many halves fit inside 4 wholes?
map.Each jar holds 2 halves, so 4 jars hold: Each jar holds 2 halves, so 4 jars hold 4 × 2 = 8 halves. 4 ÷ 1/2 = 8 torches. Dividing by a unit fraction COUNTS the pieces.
map.Sharing flips it: 2/3 of a jar split bet: Sharing works the other way: 2/3 of a jar split between 2 lamps is 2/3 × 1/2 = 1/3 of a jar each. Smaller pieces, fair shares.
map.A spare cell reads 2⁴. Expand it: 2 × 2: A spare cell reads 2⁴. Expand it: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. That is four copies of the base, all multiplied.
map.The glitch's way: 2 × 4 = 8. Wrong — the: The glitch's way: 2 × 4 = 8. Wrong! The exponent repeats the base. It never multiplies it.
map.Watch the traps: 4(m − 2) subtracts BEFO: Watch out: 4(m − 2) subtracts BEFORE multiplying. 2 − 4m flips the subtraction. Word order is the cipher.
map.Pair to judge: 5(x + 2) vs 5x + 10. Dist: Pair to judge: 5(x + 2) vs 5x + 10. Distribute: 5·x + 5·2 = 5x + 10. They match. True twins.
map.Pair: 2(x − 3) vs 2x − 3. Distribute: 2x: Pair: 2(x − 3) vs 2x − 3. Distribute: 2x − 6, which is NOT 2x − 3. The 2 must multiply the 3 as well. Fake.
map.Pair: y + y + y vs 3y. Adding three copi: Pair: y + y + y vs 3y. Adding three copies makes 3 OF them. Twins. (Multiplying three copies would be y³, a different thing.)
map.Its lights blink every 4 and every 10 tu: Its lights blink every 4 and every 10 turns. Skip-count: 4, 8, … and 10, 20, … The lists first meet at 20. LCM = 20.
map.Sanity rails: the GCF (6) is no bigger t: Check: the GCF (6) is no bigger than either gear. The LCM (20) is no smaller than either blink count. If not, you swapped them.
map.Practice seal: 3(4a + 2) = 3·4a + 3·2 =: Practice seal: 3(4a + 2) = 3·4a + 3·2 = 12a + 6. The outside number multiplies BOTH terms. 12a + 2 would be a fake.
map.That's 2 × 1/3 — multiplying makes LESS: That's 2 × 1/3. Multiplying makes LESS ink, not more lanterns. Division asks how many thirds FIT. Count slices.
map.Lock A holds. Count every third-size sli: Lock A holds. Count every third-size slice in BOTH jars of the bar model.
map.Lock A open! Now stamp Lock B — pick the: Lock A open! Now stamp Lock B. Pick the quotient of 3/4 ÷ 3.
map.2 ÷ 1/3 = 6 lanterns lit, and each hand-: 2 ÷ 1/3 = 6 lanterns lit, and each hand-lamp glows on 3/4 ÷ 3 = 1/4 jar. The stairwell BLAZES. Down we go!
map.9/4 is 3/4 × 3 — that's multiplying. Sha: 9/4 is 3/4 × 3. That is multiplying. Sharing among 3 lamps makes each share smaller than 3/4.
map.3 lamps can't each get 3 whole jars out: 3 lamps can't each get 3 whole jars out of 3/4 of one. Sharing makes the share smaller.
map.1/12 splits too far — that's dividing by: 1/12 splits too far. That is dividing by 3 twice. Share the three quarter-pieces just once.
12 is 3 × 4. Exponents repeat-multiply. Write four 3s and multiply them all.
map.10 is 2 × 5 — glitch math! The exponent: 10 is 2 × 5. That is glitch math! The exponent says multiply five 2s together.
map.3⁴ = 81 and 2⁵ = 32. Both cells flare to: 3⁴ = 81 and 2⁵ = 32. Both cells flare to life! The glitch shrieks and runs deeper into the vault!
map.Cell A stays dark. Multiply the 3s one s: Cell A stays dark. Multiply the 3s one step at a time: 3, 9, 27, …
map.Pick an expression first — the press nee: Pick an expression first. The press needs symbols before it can run.
map.3(n + 5) adds the 5 to n BEFORE tripling: 3(n + 5) adds the 5 to n BEFORE tripling. That says '3 times (5 more than n)'. Read Ada's order again.
map.5n + 3 says '3 more than 5 times n' — th: 5n + 3 says '3 more than 5 times n'. The coefficient and the constant swapped places.
map.8n smashed 3 and 5 into one coefficient: 8n squashed 3 and 5 into one coefficient. But only the 3 multiplies n. The 5 is added after.
map.3n + 5 — and at n = 4 the press prints 3: 3n + 5. And at n = 4 the press prints 3 × 4 + 5 = 17. Honest signs roll off the line!
map.27 means you added first. Multiplication: 27 means you added first. Multiplication comes before addition: triple n, THEN add.
map.Right expression! Now substitute n = 4:: Right expression! Now substitute n = 4: multiply, then add. The press waits.
map.72 is a common MULTIPLE of 24 and 36 — t: 72 is a common MULTIPLE of 24 and 36. The cog wants the greatest common FACTOR. A factor can't have more teeth than the gears it divides.
map.The cog slips. Which tooth counts divide: The cog slips. Which tooth counts divide 24 AND 36 exactly? Take the greatest one.
map.2 is the greatest common FACTOR of 6 and: 2 is the greatest common FACTOR of 6 and 8. The timing lock wants their first common MULTIPLE. Count UP, not in.
map.6 + 8 = 14 isn't on either blink list. S: 6 + 8 = 14 is not on either blink list. Skip-count by 6s and by 8s instead.
map.Lights still off-beat. Skip-count by 6s: Lights still off-beat. Skip-count by 6s and by 8s. Where do the lists first match?
map.Cog: GCF = 12 teeth. Timing: LCM = 24 tu: Cog: GCF = 12 teeth. Timing: LCM = 24 turns. KA-CHUNK! The gear heart spins true!
map.Lock 1 holds. The GCF is right! Now divi: Lock 1 holds. The GCF is right! Now divide EACH term by it: 18x ÷ 6 gives the x-term, 24 ÷ 6 gives the constant.
map.Lock 1 holds. Start with the GCF of 18 a: Lock 1 holds. Start with the GCF of 18 and 24. Then divide each term by it.
map.Lock 2 holds. Did 2³ become 6? Exponents: Lock 2 holds. Did 2³ become 6? Exponents repeat-multiply: three 2s, multiplied.
map.Lock 2 holds. Don't march straight left: Lock 2 holds. Don't go straight left to right. × and ÷ both finish BEFORE the subtraction.
map.Lock 2 holds. Order of operations: power: Lock 2 holds. Order of operations: power first, then × and ÷ left to right, subtraction last.
map.Two locks open! Stamp the equivalence se: Two locks open! Stamp the equivalence seal to finish the key.
map.Lock 3 holds. The 4 multiplied the 2n bu: Lock 3 holds. The 4 multiplied the 2n but skipped the 3. Distribute to BOTH terms.
map.Lock 3 holds. 6n + 7 is not what the 4 d: Lock 3 holds. 6n + 7 is not what the 4 does. Distributing MULTIPLIES each term by 4. It never adds.
map.Lock 3 holds. The 4 reached the 3 but mi: Lock 3 holds. The 4 reached the 3 but missed the 2n. Both terms get multiplied.
map.18x + 24 = 6(3x + 4) · code 35 · seal 8n: 18x + 24 = 6(3x + 4) · code 35 · seal 8n + 12. ALL LOCKS OPEN! The Master Key turns and the Expression Engine WAKES!
